newsitem.title: CANADA: Newbridge, Cascade seen splitting contract.
newsitem.headline: Newbridge, Cascade seen splitting contract.

text.p: Newbridge Networks Corp and rival Cascade Communications Corp appear to have divided a much-anticipated data network equipment contract from NYNEX Corp, analysts said on Wednesday.
"This whole thing is pretty much closed. We checked with some guys at NYNEX and the deal is pretty much done," said Vojtec Uzdelewicz, a networking analyst with Cowen & Co.
Analysts said Cascade "let it slip" on its post-earnings conference call last week that it had scored the asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) part of the coveted NYNEX supply deal.

"We're getting indications, and the deal hasn't been announced yet, that the frame relay portion of that contract has gone to Newbridge," Dillon Read analyst Robert MacLellan said. Speculation about the deal sent shockwaves through Newbridge stock several times last year as rumors swirled that Cascade, then a stock market darling, was going to snatch the entire contract.
"If not everybody knows about it, then it might be viewed positively for Newbridge because there was an expectation that Cascade would replace Newbridge in both ATM and frame relay," Uzdelewicz said.
"And the reality is that it's a pretty strong account for Newbridge and they got the frame relay part of the business," Uzdelewicz said.
While the contract is not enormous in dollar terms, it is important in a strategic sense, analysts said.

"I really don't know the specific contract size. The importance here of contracts like that is that the initial size is small -- you might see a US$10 (million) to US$20 million type of a deployment...But this is just the beginning of the ATM deployment and frame relay," Uzdelewicz said.

"I would expect that the potential could be in the hundreds of millions of dollars going forward. Because that's where the market is. The market is really moving toward frame relay and ATM," Uzdelewicz added.
While the victory was an important endorsement for the products of both companies, analysts said the loss of the frame relay portion could prove a negative for beleaguered Cascade.
"I think what it indicates for Cascade is the frame relay market is no longer theirs to dominate," said one analyst, who declined to be identified.

Comments from Cascade executives about slowing growth in the company's core business have sent the stock hurtling back from its previously high price-to-earnings multiple. The stock lost 23-1/8 points to end last Friday at 41.
On Wednesday, Cascade shares were 1/4 higher at 38-1/2 on Nasdaq, while Newbridge was up 0.85 at 44.65 in Toronto and 1/2 stronger at 33-1/8 in New York.
Newbridge officials declined to comment on the analysts' reports about the NYNEX deal.
